chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sakūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Regarding a man and a boy who jointly participated in killing a man and so killed him, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: If the boy has reached five spans, qiṣāṣ is carried out upon him; and if he has not reached five spans, judgment is made with the diyah.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, the source of the ruling
key_terms.اقْتُصَّ: qiṣāṣ was carried out, meaning retaliatory legal punishment
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money, the financial compensation due in place of qiṣāṣ
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَشْبَارٍ: five spans, a physical measure used here as a legal threshold
key_terms.غُلَامٍ: a boy, referring here to a minor participant in the killing
key_terms.قَتْلِ: killing, the act under legal consideration

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a boy and an adult jointly kill a man?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man and a boy who jointly kill another man. It distinguishes between whether the boy has reached a specified physical measure, making qiṣāṣ applicable, or else requiring diyah instead.
